draft.title: Non-religious worldviews
card: Atheism
the rejection of belief in God or gods. An atheist holds that no god exists.
Agnosticism
the view that it cannot be known whether God exists, because there is not enough evidence either way. An agnostic does not claim to know.
Humanism
a worldview that finds meaning and ethics in human reason, experience and shared values, not in a god. Many humanists are also atheists or agnostics.
Atheism and agnosticism are about belief in God. Humanism is about where meaning and ethics come from.
draft.remember: Atheists reject belief in God, agnostics say it cannot be known, and humanists look to human reason and values for meaning.

a.q: Which view holds that it cannot be known whether God exists?
a.why: Agnosticism says the evidence does not allow anyone to know either way. Atheism is the tempting wrong answer, because it goes further and rejects belief in God.
a.clue: Which view makes no claim to know?

b.q: Priya says she does not believe any god exists. She also says people can build a good life using reason and care for others. Which pair of terms fits her views?
opts: Humanism only, as it rejects belief in God
b.why: Priya rejects belief in God, which is atheism, and finds meaning in reason and care for others, which is humanism. Agnosticism does not fit, because she states that no god exists instead of saying it cannot be known.
b.clue: Does she say no god exists, or that it cannot be known?

problems.detail: The stem says Priya 'does not believe any god exists'. That describes a lack of belief, which an agnostic could also say. It does not match the card's definition of an atheist as someone who 'holds that no god exists', and the why claims 'she states that no god exists', which the stem does not say. Rewording the stem to 'she believes no god exists' would make the atheism reading clear.
